title: Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections
bottleneck: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii and Enterobacterales top WHO's critical-priority pathogen list; they cause bloodstream and ventilator-associated infections with mortality often exceeding 40%, and treatment options are limited to toxic or partially effective last-resort agents.
why_it_blocks: Gram-negative bacteria's double membrane makes drug discovery intrinsically hard; resistance to last-resort carbapenems removes the final safety net for common hospital infections.
current_state: New beta-lactam and beta-lactamase inhibitor combinations have helped, but only a handful of pipeline agents target critical Gram-negatives, and resistance to each new agent emerges within years of introduction. Infection-control measures in hospitals can slow spread but cannot substitute for effective drugs. Each new agent buys only a few years before resistance emerges, making the innovation treadmill brutally short, and the pipeline behind them is nearly empty.
